title: Player Controls, Timeline Scrubber & Parameter Control Architecture

This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/PLAYER_CONTROLS_AND_TIMELINE_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/PLAYER_CONTROLS_AND_TIMELINE_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Retiam provides built-in DOM controls for interactive inspection, playback choreography, and live parameter adjustment during development and scene presentation:

items: **[`PlayerControls`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/control/PlayerControls.ts)**: A sleek, dark-mode timeline player bar mounted over the canvas that provides video player mechanics (play, pause, scrub, step, speed tuning, fullscreen, looping).

**[`ControlPanel`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/control/menu.ts)**: A lightweight, collapsible HUD parameter tweaker for modifying numbers, scalars, vectors, and boolean toggles in real time without recompilation.

blocks.text: The `PlayerControls` class attaches to a [`Scene`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Scene.ts) instance and interfaces directly with the scene's timeline state machine:

children.label: PlayerControls
children.description: DOM transport bar; keeps playback state synchronized with the scene.

items: **Interactive Timeline Scrubber**: A smoothed range slider showing playback progress ($t \in [0, T_{\text{total}}]$). Scrubbing temporarily pauses continuous rendering and calls `scene.seekTo(targetTime)` for zero-latency frame preview.

**Granular Frame Stepping**: Left and Right navigation buttons (or arrow keys) step through time by exact frame increments ($\Delta t = 1 / 60\text{s}$ or configurable frame rate), allowing animators to audit sub-second transitions.

**Variable Playback Rate**: Speed control dropdown supporting multipliers ($0.25\times, 0.5\times, 1.0\times, 1.5\times, 2.0\times$), scaling the time delta $\Delta t$ fed to the scene composition loop.
**Loop Boundaries**: Allows looping the scene continuously between custom start and end points ($t_{\text{start}} \to t_{\text{end}}$), indispensable for tuning cyclic mathematical animations.

children: `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`: Step backward / forward 1 frame (or $\pm 1\text{s}$ when holding Shift).
`F`: Toggle true fullscreen canvas mode with automatic aspect ratio preservation.
`Home` / `End`: Jump to scene start ($t=0$) or scene end ($t=T_{\text{total}}$).

blocks.text: The `ControlPanel` provides an embeddable, draggable parameter HUD for interactive demonstrations, math experiments, and live presentations:

The control panel automatically generates and injects scoped CSS (`control-panel-styles`) into the `<head>` of the host document on instantiation. It features glassmorphism styling, clean modern typography, accent range sliders, collapsible minimize headers, and mobile-friendly touch targets.
